question: Which artist has the highest popularity score and how many albums have they released?
sql_query:
SELECT a.name, a.popularity_score, COUNT(DISTINCT al.album_id) as album_count
FROM artists a
LEFT JOIN albums al ON a.artist_id = al.artist_id
WHERE a.popularity_score = (SELECT MAX(popularity_score) FROM artists)
GROUP BY a.artist_id, a.name, a.popularity_score;

question: What is the total revenue generated from royalties in Q4-2024?
Which music genre has the most tracks and how many?
sql_query:
SELECT a.primary_genre, COUNT(t.track_id) as track_count
FROM tracks t
JOIN artists a ON t.artist_id = a.artist_id
GROUP BY a.primary_genre
ORDER BY track_count DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: What percentage of artists are currently inactive?
Which streaming platform has the highest total stream count?

FROM streams

question: What is the average track duration in minutes across all tracks?
sql_query:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(duration_ms) / 1000.0 / 60.0, 2) as avg_duration_minutes

question: How many collaborations involve Hip-Hop artists as the primary artist?
sql_query:
SELECT COUNT(c.collab_id) as hiphop_collaborations
FROM collaborations c
JOIN artists a ON c.primary_artist_id = a.artist_id

question: Which record label has signed the most artists and what type of label is it?
sql_query:
SELECT rl.name, rl.label_type, COUNT(a.artist_id) as artist_count
FROM record_labels rl
JOIN artists a ON rl.label_id = a.label_id
GROUP BY rl.label_id, rl.name, rl.label_type
ORDER BY artist_count DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: What is the average energy level of Electronic music tracks?
sql_query:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(tf.energy), 3) as avg_energy
FROM track_features tf
JOIN tracks t ON tf.track_id = t.track_id
JOIN artists a ON t.artist_id = a.artist_id
WHERE a.primary_genre = 'Electronic';

question: How many awards has the most awarded artist won (not just nominated)?
sql_query:
SELECT a.name, COUNT(*) as awards_won
FROM awards aw
JOIN artists a ON aw.artist_id = a.artist_id
WHERE aw.won = true
GROUP BY aw.artist_id, a.name
ORDER BY awards_won DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: What is the total number of streams for tracks released in 2024?
sql_query:

FROM streams s
JOIN tracks t ON s.track_id = t.track_id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.release_date) = 2024;

question: Which country has produced the most Rock artists?

question: Which artist has the best streams-to-awards ratio (total streams divided by number of awards won), considering only artists with at least 5 awards won?
sql_query:
SELECT a.name, 
    SUM(s.stream_count) as total_streams,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN aw.won = true THEN aw.award_id END) as awards_won,
    ROUND(SUM(s.stream_count)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN aw.won = true THEN aw.award_id END), 2) as streams_per_award
FROM artists a
JOIN streams s ON a.artist_id = s.artist_id
JOIN awards aw ON a.artist_id = aw.artist_id
WHERE aw.won = true
GROUP BY a.artist_id, a.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN aw.won = true THEN aw.award_id END) >= 5
ORDER BY streams_per_award DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: What is the correlation between track danceability and average stream count? Show the average stream count for tracks grouped by danceability ranges (0-0.3, 0.3-0.6, 0.6-1.0).
sql_query:
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN tf.danceability < 0.3 THEN 'Low (0-0.3)'
        WHEN tf.danceability < 0.6 THEN 'Medium (0.3-0.6)'
        ELSE 'High (0.6-1.0)'
    END as danceability_range,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.track_id) as track_count,
    ROUND(AVG(s.stream_count), 0) as avg_streams
FROM track_features tf
JOIN tracks t ON tf.track_id = t.track_id
JOIN streams s ON t.track_id = s.track_id
GROUP BY danceability_range
ORDER BY danceability_range;

question: Which label generates the highest average revenue per artist, and what is that amount? Include only labels with at least 10 artists.
sql_query:
SELECT rl.name, rl.label_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id) as artist_count,
    ROUND(SUM(r.gross_revenue_usd) / COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id), 2) as avg_revenue_per_artist
FROM record_labels rl
JOIN artists a ON rl.label_id = a.label_id
JOIN royalties r ON a.artist_id = r.artist_id
GROUP BY rl.label_id, rl.name, rl.label_type
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id) >= 10
ORDER BY avg_revenue_per_artist DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: Find the top 3 most "collaborative" genres - genres where artists have the highest average number of collaborations per artist.
sql_query:
SELECT a.primary_genre,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id) as total_artists,
    COUNT(c.collab_id) as total_collaborations,
    ROUND(COUNT(c.collab_id)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id), 2) as avg_collabs_per_artist
FROM artists a
LEFT JOIN collaborations c ON a.artist_id = c.primary_artist_id
GROUP BY a.primary_genre
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id) >= 30
ORDER BY avg_collabs_per_artist DESC
LIMIT 3;

question: Which track has been on the charts for the longest cumulative time across all chart types, and how many total weeks?
sql_query:
SELECT t.title, t.track_id, a.name as artist_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.chart_name) as chart_appearances,
    SUM(c.weeks_on_chart) as total_weeks_on_charts
FROM charts c
JOIN tracks t ON c.track_id = t.track_id
JOIN artists a ON t.artist_id = a.artist_id
GROUP BY t.track_id, t.title, a.name
ORDER BY total_weeks_on_charts DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: What is the month-over-month growth rate of streaming in 2024? Show the total streams for each month and the percentage change from the previous month.
sql_query:
WITH monthly_streams AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', stream_date) as month,
        SUM(stream_count) as total_streams
    FROM streams
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM stream_date) = 2024
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', stream_date)
)
SELECT 
    TO_CHAR(month, 'YYYY-MM') as month,
    total_streams,
    LAG(total_streams) OVER (ORDER BY month) as prev_month_streams,
    ROUND(100.0 * (total_streams - LAG(total_streams) OVER (ORDER BY month)) / 
          NULLIF(LAG(total_streams) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) as growth_rate_pct
FROM monthly_streams
ORDER BY month;

question: Calculate the "virality coefficient" for each genre: (average chart peak position × average weeks on chart × total awards won) / average completion rate. Which genre has the highest coefficient?
sql_query:
WITH genre_metrics AS (
    SELECT a.primary_genre,
        AVG(ch.peak_position) as avg_peak_position,
        AVG(ch.weeks_on_chart) as avg_weeks_on_chart,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN aw.won = true THEN aw.award_id END) as total_awards_won,
        AVG(s.completion_rate) as avg_completion_rate
    FROM artists a
    LEFT JOIN tracks t ON a.artist_id = t.artist_id
    LEFT JOIN charts ch ON t.track_id = ch.track_id
    LEFT JOIN awards aw ON a.artist_id = aw.artist_id
    LEFT JOIN streams s ON t.track_id = s.track_id
    WHERE s.completion_rate IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY a.primary_genre
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.track_id) >= 100
)
SELECT primary_genre,
    ROUND(avg_peak_position, 2) as avg_peak,
    ROUND(avg_weeks_on_chart, 2) as avg_weeks,
    total_awards_won,
    ROUND(avg_completion_rate, 3) as avg_completion,
    ROUND((avg_peak_position * avg_weeks_on_chart * total_awards_won) / NULLIF(avg_completion_rate, 0), 2) as virality_coefficient
FROM genre_metrics
ORDER BY virality_coefficient DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: Find the "hidden gems" - tracks with high completion rates (>85%) but low popularity scores (<0.05) that have never charted. How many such tracks exist and what is their total stream count?
sql_query:
WITH track_metrics AS (
    SELECT t.track_id, t.title, t.popularity_score,
        AVG(s.completion_rate) as avg_completion_rate,
        SUM(s.stream_count) as total_streams,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ch.chart_id) as chart_count
    FROM tracks t
    JOIN streams s ON t.track_id = s.track_id
    LEFT JOIN charts ch ON t.track_id = ch.track_id
    GROUP BY t.track_id, t.title, t.popularity_score
    HAVING AVG(s.completion_rate) > 0.85 
        AND t.popularity_score < 0.05
        AND COUNT(DISTINCT ch.chart_id) = 0
)
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) as hidden_gem_count,
    SUM(total_streams) as total_hidden_gem_streams,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_completion_rate), 3) as avg_completion_rate,
    ROUND(AVG(popularity_score), 4) as avg_popularity
FROM track_metrics;

question: Analyze the "collaboration network effect": For artists with 10+ collaborations, calculate the average popularity boost (difference between their popularity and the average popularity of artists they collaborated with). Which artist has the highest positive network effect?
sql_query:
WITH artist_collab_metrics AS (
    SELECT c.primary_artist_id,
        a1.name as primary_artist_name,
        a1.popularity_score as primary_popularity,
        COUNT(c.collab_id) as collab_count,
        AVG(a2.popularity_score) as avg_collaborator_popularity
    FROM collaborations c
    JOIN artists a1 ON c.primary_artist_id = a1.artist_id
    JOIN artists a2 ON c.featured_artist_id = a2.artist_id
    GROUP BY c.primary_artist_id, a1.name, a1.popularity_score
    HAVING COUNT(c.collab_id) >= 10
)
SELECT primary_artist_name,
    collab_count,
    ROUND(primary_popularity, 4) as own_popularity,
    ROUND(avg_collaborator_popularity, 4) as avg_collab_popularity,
    ROUND(primary_popularity - avg_collaborator_popularity, 4) as network_effect
FROM artist_collab_metrics
ORDER BY network_effect DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: Calculate the "revenue efficiency ratio" for each label type (Major/Independent/Subsidiary): total artist payout divided by (number of artists × average years active). Which label type is most efficient?
sql_query:
WITH label_metrics AS (
    SELECT rl.label_type,
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id) as artist_count,
        SUM(r.artist_payout_usd) as total_artist_payout,
        AVG(2024 - a.debut_year) as avg_years_active
    FROM record_labels rl
    JOIN artists a ON rl.label_id = a.label_id
    JOIN royalties r ON a.artist_id = r.artist_id
    GROUP BY rl.label_type
)
SELECT label_type,
    artist_count,
    ROUND(total_artist_payout, 2) as total_payout,
    ROUND(avg_years_active, 2) as avg_years_active,
    ROUND(total_artist_payout / (artist_count * avg_years_active), 2) as efficiency_ratio
FROM label_metrics
ORDER BY efficiency_ratio DESC;

question: Identify the "Midas touch" producer - the featured artist in "Producer" type collaborations whose tracks have the highest average chart peak position (lower is better). Include only producers involved in at least 5 collaborations.
sql_query:
WITH producer_performance AS (
    SELECT a.name as producer_name,
        a.artist_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT c.collab_id) as production_count,
        AVG(ch.peak_position) as avg_peak_position,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ch.chart_id) as charting_tracks
    FROM collaborations c
    JOIN artists a ON c.featured_artist_id = a.artist_id
    JOIN tracks t ON c.track_id = t.track_id
    LEFT JOIN charts ch ON t.track_id = ch.track_id
    WHERE c.collab_type = 'Producer'
    GROUP BY a.artist_id, a.name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.collab_id) >= 5
        AND COUNT(DISTINCT ch.chart_id) > 0
)
SELECT producer_name,
    production_count,
    charting_tracks,
    ROUND(avg_peak_position, 2) as avg_peak_position
FROM producer_performance
ORDER BY avg_peak_position ASC
LIMIT 1;

question: Create a "genre evolution timeline": For each genre, calculate the average popularity score of artists by their debut decade (1990s, 2000s, 2010s, 2020s). Which genre shows the most consistent growth (highest correlation between decade and popularity)?
sql_query:
WITH genre_decade_popularity AS (
    SELECT primary_genre,
        CASE 
            WHEN debut_year BETWEEN 1990 AND 1999 THEN '1990s'
            WHEN debut_year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2009 THEN '2000s'
            WHEN debut_year BETWEEN 2010 AND 2019 THEN '2010s'
            WHEN debut_year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2029 THEN '2020s'
        END as debut_decade,
        AVG(popularity_score) as avg_popularity,
        COUNT(*) as artist_count
    FROM artists
    WHERE debut_year >= 1990
    GROUP BY primary_genre, debut_decade
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
)
SELECT primary_genre,
    STRING_AGG(debut_decade || ': ' || ROUND(avg_popularity, 4)::text, ', ' ORDER BY debut_decade) as popularity_by_decade,
    MAX(CASE WHEN debut_decade = '2020s' THEN avg_popularity ELSE 0 END) - 
    MIN(CASE WHEN debut_decade = '1990s' THEN avg_popularity ELSE 999 END) as growth_indicator
FROM genre_decade_popularity
GROUP BY primary_genre
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT debut_decade) >= 3
ORDER BY growth_indicator DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: Calculate the "playlist power index" for each platform: (number of public playlists × average position in playlist) / total unique users. Which platform has the highest index, indicating better playlist curation?
sql_query:
WITH platform_metrics AS (
    SELECT platform,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN is_public = true THEN 1 END) as public_playlist_count,
        AVG(position) as avg_position,
        COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) as unique_users,
        COUNT(*) as total_entries
    FROM playlists
    GROUP BY platform
)
SELECT platform,
    public_playlist_count,
    ROUND(avg_position, 2) as avg_position,
    unique_users,
    ROUND((public_playlist_count * avg_position)::numeric / unique_users, 2) as playlist_power_index
FROM platform_metrics
ORDER BY playlist_power_index DESC
LIMIT 1;

question: Find the "undervalued" label - the label with the highest ratio of (total streams generated by their artists) to (total royalties paid to those artists), considering only labels with at least 15 artists. This indicates which label is getting the most streaming value for their investment.
sql_query:
WITH label_performance AS (
    SELECT rl.label_id,
        rl.name as label_name,
        rl.label_type,
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id) as artist_count,
        SUM(s.stream_count) as total_streams,
        SUM(r.artist_payout_usd) as total_artist_payout,
        SUM(r.label_cut_usd) as total_label_revenue
    FROM record_labels rl
    JOIN artists a ON rl.label_id = a.label_id
    JOIN streams s ON a.artist_id = s.artist_id
    JOIN royalties r ON a.artist_id = r.artist_id
    GROUP BY rl.label_id, rl.name, rl.label_type
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.artist_id) >= 15
)
SELECT label_name,
    label_type,
    artist_count,
    total_streams,
    ROUND(total_artist_payout, 2) as total_payout,
    ROUND(total_label_revenue, 2) as label_revenue,
    ROUND(total_streams::numeric / NULLIF(total_artist_payout, 0), 2) as streams_per_dollar_paid
FROM label_performance
ORDER BY streams_per_dollar_paid DESC
LIMIT 1;
